grammar.title: Expressing certainty with 一定
grammar.explanation: 一定 (yídìng) means "surely, certainly" and shows strong confidence. It goes right before the verb. In a request, 一定要 means "must, be sure to".

grammar.title: Continuous action with 一直
grammar.explanation: 一直 (yìzhí) means "continuously, all along" and describes an action that keeps happening without stopping. It sits before the verb, and is often paired with 都 for extra emphasis.

sentences.pinyin: Zhè běn shū yídìng hěn yǒumíng.
sentences.en: This book must be very famous.
He has been reading the whole time.

sentences.zh: 我一直很喜欢这个学校。
sentences.pinyin: Wǒ yìzhí hěn xǐhuan zhège xuéxiào.

sentences.en: She hasn't said anything the whole time.

sentences.pinyin: Zhème duō cài, wǒ chī bu liǎo.
sentences.en: That's so much food, I can't finish it.

sentences.zh: 我的包放不下这么多书。
sentences.pinyin: Wǒ de bāo fàng bu xià zhème duō shū.
sentences.en: My bag can't hold this many books.
